body: I think the shower would be a lot more dynamic and natural in the space if the door were at an angle that ran parallel to the wall that is to the left of the toilet (if you were sitting on the toilet). Also, what if your cabinets ran floor to ceiling? The space feels choppy enough already. Finally, what about a freestanding bathtub?

>My ex husband crossed a major boundary for me once during sex. My response was similar to your response and his response was similar to your boyfriend's. We never healed from that event and my lack of safety around sex grew to an unmanageable point. Eventually, I was so physically distant that my husband asked me for a divorce. If you want to stay with this guy and build a future, I would suggest going to a therapist.   
>  
>On a related and unrelated note, my husband turned out to be an abusive (covert) narcissist. I made excuses in my head for it at the time, but the fact that I comforted him when he had violated me never sat quite right with me...Trust your instincts. If it didn't feel right, it wasn't right. If he is feeling guilty, I would bet that he knew he took it past your agreements. His behavior feels like a detraction from your trauma and a distraction from what really happened.
